title: egy vagy a? Choosing Indefinite or Definite Past

sections.title: The same test, every time
sections.content: Whatever verb you're using — vesz, lát, olvas, anything transitive — the test for which past ending to use never changes: look at the object. egy + noun, or no article at all, means the object is unspecified, so the verb takes the indefinite ending. a/az + noun, a possessive (a kabátom), or a name (Tamást) all mean the object is specific, so the verb takes the definite ending — even in a sentence that's otherwise entirely new vocabulary.

sections.title: Indefinite or definite?
rows: definite — the specific one you gave me

items.english: I bought a wonderful gift for Zsófia.

items.spanish: Megvettem a csodálatos ajándékot, amit a kirakatban láttam.
items.english: I bought the wonderful gift I saw in the shop window.

items.spanish: Meséltél nekem egy érdekes történetet, de már elfelejtettem.
items.english: You told me an interesting story, but I've already forgotten it.

sections.content: When you're not sure which ending to reach for, ask yourself: could I point at exactly one thing right now? If yes, it's definite — even without the word a in front, the way a name always is.
